items.title: anymove
items.description: Motion capture for any creature from one AI video: two cameras in one frame, a DINOv2 joint reader, the rig fitted in both views, a GLB out.
items.summary: anymove is an open-source motion capture tool that turns one AI-generated video of a creature filmed from two angles into a rigged, animated 3D character. The process involves a video model filming the creature from two cameras in one frame, a joint reader trained on the creature to find every joint in both views, and a rig fitted to those joints frame by frame, which is then exported as a GLB file. The output is a ready-to-use GLB file at 24fps with no hand edits, and each new move costs about $0.26. The method is based on @CanItCode’s work, and the MiniMax LoRA step was another creator’s idea.

items.title: teachable-figures
items.description: An agent skill for causal teaching figures through predict, try, and explain. Includes rendering kits, reviewed examples, and browser checks.
items.summary: The teachable-figures agent skill is designed for interactive learning through a predict, try, and explain loop. It turns a hard-to-grasp claim into an offline interactive figure where learners predict, change one cause, observe the effect, and explain it in their own words. The skill fuses existing teaching workflows with rendering skills and includes rendering examples and verification tools. It works with a host application's lesson schema or a standalone HTML figure. The skill is used by agents like Claude Code and Codex and includes reviewed examples and browser checks.

items.title: cheap-ag
items.description: 50x your usage with cheap-ag. Opus/Astra plans, a dirt-cheap model writes every line, and tests decide what ships. Your $20 plan stops hitting limits. One MCP server for Claude Code & Codex.
items.summary: The sources indicate that the $20 Pro tier of Claude Code provides 10-20 meaningful coding sessions per week, with heavy users often hitting limits by midweek. The Max 5x ($100/month) and Max 20x ($200/month) plans offer increased usage limits, with the Max 5x plan providing 5x the Pro tier's usage and the Max 20x plan offering 20x the Pro tier's usage. The Pro tier uses Sonnet 4.6 by default, while the Max tiers use Opus 4.6. The exact message count ceiling for the Max 5x plan is not specified. The sources do not provide a definitive answer regarding the specific multiplier for the Max 5x plan in terms of message counts.

items.title: vn-law-check
items.description: Audit pháp lý website theo luật Việt Nam (BVDLCN 91/2025, TMĐT 122/2025, ANM 116/2025, AI 134/2025) cho Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, Cline
items.summary: The sources indicate that Vietnam's Law on Artificial Intelligence, effective March 1, 2026, is the first standalone binding AI law in Southeast Asia. It introduces a risk-based classification system, registration requirements, and penalties up to VND 2 billion for non-compliance. The law comprises 35 articles and 8 chapters regulating AI activities, including the rights and obligations of organizations and individuals, and state management of AI activities in Vietnam. The law's effective date is March 1, 2026, and AI systems in operation must fulfill obligations within 12-18 months, depending on the field.

items.title: sound

items.summary: The sources mention Freesound as a platform for sound effects, but they do not provide specific information about studio-grade sound effects for agents or rank them by human feedback. Freesound is described as a private company based in Barcelona, Spain, with a website at www.freesound.org. The other sources discuss AI sound effect generators and their features but do not directly address the search for studio-grade sound effects from Pixabay, Freesound, Mixkit, and Kenney.

items.title: verdict
items.description: A 197 KB local semantic verifier for AI agent tool calls. Exit code 0 is not proof.
items.summary: The sources indicate that a 197 KB local semantic verifier for AI agent tool calls is part of a method that significantly reduces duplicate actions and maintains comparable task success rates by augmenting tool calls with postcondition verification, verify-before-retry logic, and idempotency keys. However, exit code 0 is not proof of the verifier's effectiveness, as the sources do not provide definitive evidence that it alone guarantees reliability. The sources also highlight the importance of permissions and configuration in tool invocation, and the need for semantic validation to handle incorrect data returned by tools.

items.title: roblox-ai-studio-agent
items.description: An AI agent in your terminal that builds Roblox places in Studio: parts, models, UI and Luau scripts. Place diff before every change, playtests with proof, one undo per turn.
items.summary: The sources describe an AI agent for Roblox Studio that builds places in Studio, including parts, models, UI, and Luau scripts. It emphasizes safe edits with place diffs before changes, playtests with proof, and one undo per turn. Another source highlights the agent's ability to generate and edit Luau scripts, build game objects, create animations, debug code, validate projects, and test features before reporting success. The third source details features like direct Studio control, script editing, AI tools, multi-provider support, live feedback, and undo support. The premise of the agent's existence is supported by the sources, but specific details like official names or URLs are not provided.

items.title: readme-visual-kit
items.description: 把带源码依据的项目说明变成三张 README 图：功能流程、简化架构、快速上手。本地 SVG 渲染器 + Agent Skill，无需 API Key。
items.summary: The readme-visual-kit is an open-source AI agent skill designed to convert project documentation based on source code into three unified style diagrams: functional flow, simplified architecture, and quick start guide. It utilizes a local SVG renderer and a portable Agent Skill, requiring no API key or third-party dependencies. The tool is built by tianfuzhibuyuci and has 169 GitHub stars. It is not an online AI service but a local MVP, and its examples are demonstration programs, not indicative of third-party use or commercial adoption.

items.title: airhand
items.description: High-performance remote desktop over QUIC · Rust + Tauri + React
items.summary: The sources indicate that the project "entagle" is an open-source, low-latency remote desktop built with Rust, Tauri, and QUIC. It features a high-level workspace architecture, signaling server, frontend scaffolding with React and Shadcn UI, and uses WebCodecs API for video decoding. The tech stack includes Rust, QUIC (quinn), WebSockets (axum), Tauri v2 for the desktop client, and React with Vite and TypeScript for the frontend. The project is also implementing platform-native screen capture and video encoding abstractions. The YouTube video discusses building a production-ready desktop app in Rust using Tauri 2.0, Axum, and TanStack for React, emphasizing a small binary size and modern UI with React and Tailwind CSS. The blog post on building cross-platform desktop apps with Tauri 2.0 details the use of the #[command] macro for callable commands from the frontend and the invocation of these commands using Tauri's JavaScript API.

items.title: ai-design-check
items.description: Design rules and a zero-dependency checker for interfaces built with AI coding agents, on the web and in SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose apps. English and Turkish.
items.summary: The sources describe "ai-design-check" as a tool that provides design rules and a zero-dependency checker for interfaces built with AI coding agents, supporting both web and mobile applications built with SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose. It is available in English and Turkish, and the rules it enforces include spacing, radii, text size, headings, gradients, and other design elements. The tool can be installed via `npx @enmera/ai-design-check` and applied to specific app folders to check for design rule violations. The rules are defined in `rules.json` and can include class patterns, regex patterns, or structural checks. The sources do not provide a definitive answer regarding specific rules or the full list of design rules enforced by the tool.

items.title: minecraft-ai-mod-builder
items.description: Type what you want built, see it as a blueprint in your Minecraft world, place it in one step and undo it in one. Fabric companion, Paper plugin, free local models, one Windows build.
items.summary: The sources indicate that EnderDevelopment offers an AI Mod Maker for Minecraft that allows users to create mods for Forge and Fabric without coding, trained on working mods to generate production-ready code. Player Games' AI Minecraft mod maker turns descriptions into working mods, supports Fabric, NeoForge, Spigot, Paper, and data packs, and boots every build on a real Minecraft server before download. It provides the source code along with the compiled JAR. Both tools support Fabric and Paper, with Player Games additionally supporting NeoForge, Spigot, and data packs. Neither source provides a definitive answer to the specific request for a one-step place-and-undo feature, a Windows-only build, or a Fabric companion plugin.

items.title: weeping-of-the-empire
items.description: Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom (TotK) 1.0.0 recompiled to native Windows and Vulkan. Frame cap up to 240, DLSS option, mouse and keyboard. Open source, mostly written by AI agents. You build it from your own dump; no game files included. Measured on one PC so far.
items.summary: The “Weeping‑of‑the‑Empire” project is an unofficial native Windows port of *Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom* (TotK) 1.4.3 that uses static recompilation. It is built locally from a player’s own extracted game dump and contains no game files. The source code is open‑source and largely written by AI agents. It supports frame rates of 30, 60, 90, 120 or unlocked (up to the monitor’s refresh rate, 240 fps at most) while running at the game’s real speed, any window size and render resolution, ultrawide, borderless or exclusive fullscreen, VRR, HDR, and offers upscaling options including NVIDIA DLSS super‑resolution on RTX cards, DLSS frame generation on RTX 40/50 series, FSR 1, and SMAA.
